:::{#def-probability-space}
#### Probability space

For a probability measure $\P$ (@def-probability-measure) on a [measurable space](#def-measurable-space) $(\samplespace, \events)$,
$(\samplespace, \events, \P)$ is a **probability space**.
[@wikipedia_probability_space]

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-sample-space}
#### Sample space

In a probability space $(\samplespace, \events, \P)$ (@def-probability-space),
$\samplespace$ is its **sample space**.
[@wikipedia_sample_space]

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-outcome}
#### Outcome

In a probability space $(\samplespace, \events, \P)$ (@def-probability-space),
the elements of the sample space $\samplespace$ (@def-sample-space) are **outcomes**.
[@wikipedia_outcome_probability]

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-event}
#### Event

In a probability space $(\samplespace, \events, \P)$ (@def-probability-space),
the sets in $\events$ are **events**.
[@wikipedia_event_probability_theory]

:::
